## IA drift review

All three findings are real but none break runtime — they create conditions for agent and user confusion. My recommendation for each:

### crime_00017 — route_metadata_drift → **WARN** (block if PR touches `/settings/billing`)
Five divergent labels on one route:
- file `billing.tsx` · component `PricingPage` · `metadata.title: Plans` · `<title>: Subscription` · nav labels `Plans` vs `Billing`

This is the load-bearing finding of the three. Real UX hazard (a user clicking "Billing" in the sidebar lands on a page titled "Subscription" rendered by `PricingPage`), and exactly the kind of state an agent silently makes worse — fix one surface, the other four stay stale. Confidence is only 0.65 because some divergence could be an in-progress rename, so don't auto-block, but if any PR touches the route file or either nav source, escalate to block until the team picks one canonical name and aligns.

### crime_00015 — duplicated_navigation_source → **WARN** (same change as #17, not a separate task)
`/settings/billing` in `nav/registry.ts` as "Plans" and `nav/sidebar.ts` as "Billing". This is a strict subset of #17 — the visible symptom of the same root cause. Track it as part of the route-metadata fix, not as its own ticket. Picking a canonical label here resolves the route-drift evidence line about nav labels.

The deeper fix is structural: collapse to one nav source of truth (or document which file is canonical and have the other derive). Don't fix the labels without that, or the drift will return.

### crime_00013 — docs_code_drift → **WARN** (cheap; don't ignore)
`docs/teams.md:5 → ./setup.md (not found)`. Low severity, but two reasons not to downgrade to ignore:

1. The repo also has **crime_00006 missing_agent_context** (no AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / SKILL.md). Agents loading this repo will lean harder on docs/ for orientation, and broken links there are higher-leverage than they look.
2. Cost to fix is one line — either restore `setup.md` or correct the link. The ratio of fix-cost to confusion-cost is favourable.

If the team treats `docs/` as deliberately draft (rare), then ignore — but flag the assumption.

### Summary

| Finding | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| route_metadata_drift | warn → block if touched | Root cause; pick canonical name |
| duplicated_navigation_source | warn (fix with #17) | Same change, don't track twice |
| docs_code_drift | warn | Cheap; agents will follow stale link |

No outright blocks — none of these break the build or runtime. But #17 + #15 should be addressed together as a small structural change, not three label edits.
